Daily Current Affairs 21 August 2026

1. Elon Musk's Starlink pitches its services to significantly boost high-speed internet connectivity across rural regions in India. [Source: The Indian Express]
2. India successfully dismantles multiple unauthorised structures located directly outside the Pakistan High Commission. [Source: The Indian Express]
3. NEET UG 2026 counselling announces Round 1 final seat allotment featuring 31,728 seats, with reporting starting August 22. [Source: Bhaskar English]
4. Delhi University (DU) undergraduate applications officially close today, with the much-anticipated merit list scheduled for August 23 release. [Source: Bhaskar English]
5. Severe floods severely impact four blocks in Bhadrak, leading to emergency closures of 518 schools across Bhadrak and Jajpur districts. [Source: Kanak News Odisha]
6. Authorities in Bhubaneswar successfully raid and seize a massive stock of fake paneer in a major food safety crackdown. [Source: Kanak News Odisha]
7. Over 130 villages remain completely cut off following rising floodwaters in the Bhograi region, alongside local relief operations. [Source: Kanak News Odisha]
8. Jharkhand opposition strongly objects to provisions of the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) or MMDR Bill. [Source: Kanak News Odisha]
9. Punjab observes a bandh as various political and social groups demonstrate over prominent socio-political demands today. [Source: Jagran Josh]
10. The official Aadhaar mobile application reaches a major usage milestone, registering record-breaking authentication numbers nationwide. [Source: Jagran Josh]
11. Educational authorities order immediate closure of schools across specified districts in Manipur keeping student safety in view. [Source: Jagran Josh]
12. School assembly headlines highlight ongoing national developments, economic updates, and crucial regional news across India. [Source: The Economic Times]
13. Educational institutions nationwide feature current national affairs, international relations, and competitive sports updates for morning assemblies. [Source: India Today]
14. Morning news bulletins for students cover essential updates ranging from domestic infrastructure projects to major international diplomatic events. [Source: The Daily Jagran]
